newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court okays extradition of top Basque.
newsitem.headline: French court okays extradition of top Basque.

text.p: A French appeals court on Wednesday authorised the extradition to Spain of former Basque guerrilla leader Santiago Arrospide Sarasola, whom Madrid alleges masterminded several bloody bomb attacks, court sources said.
They said the court in Versailles had ruled that the former guerrilla, better known as Santi Potros, could be extradited in connection with "destruction by explosives".
The ruling gave no details of the charges. The extradition still needs to be approved by the government.

The 48-year-old former ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) leader faces charges in Spain of ordering several attacks, including a car-bomb explosion at a Barcelona supermarket in 1987 which killed 20 people.

French courts had rejected several previous extradition requests. Santi Potros was believed to be the number two in ETA, a guerrilla group which has killed hundreds of people in Spain in its campaign for a separate Basque state.
He was detained in France in 1987 and three years later was jailed for 10 years for guerrilla activities.
European Union justice ministers last week signed a convention to tighten cooperation on extradition to prevent people suspected of terrorism in one EU member state walking free in another.

French President Jacques Chirac, who hardened the fight against ETA when he was prime minister in 1986-88, ordered still greater cooperation with Madrid against the guerrillas after fellow conservative Jose Maria Aznar took over as Spanish prime minister last May.
